title: Customer Payments, Refunds and Credits — Insurance Claim Repairs Accounting Rules
content:
## Payments

Customer payments reduce an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order's customer balance and may be made at any time before or at delivery, by the class's accepted payment methods. Financing through the network's partner is offered only where the class makes financing available and the balance being financed is at least the class's financing minimum.

| Financing available in the class | Balance to be financed compared with the class minimum | Financing offered |
|---|---|---|
| yes | at or above the minimum | yes |
| yes | below the minimum | no |
| no | any | no |

## Refunds of overpayments

The clause providing that, when payments exceed what is owed (the customer balance below zero), the excess is refunded to the method of the payment being refunded within the class's refund processing business days, one refund per payment and never more than that payment, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current refund basis.

The refund names the payment it returns. The name is checked against the repair order's money history before the refund is recorded: a payment that an existing refund already names is not refunded again.

## Credits

Credits name the charge they reduce and never exceed it. The credit reasons are:

| Credit reason | Governed by |
|---|---|
| billing error | corrects a charge posted at the wrong amount |
| total-loss release | the total-loss rule |
| repair withdrawn | the vehicle withdrawal rule |
| addition withdrawn | the customer-pay additions rule |
| goodwill | the storage rule |

*Hypothetical:* a storage charge of USD 135.00 was posted where USD 90.00 was due. A billing-error credit of USD 45.00 names that storage charge; a credit of USD 150.00 against it would exceed the charge and is not made.

superseded_clauses: When payments exceed what is owed (claim_msr_customer_balance below zero), the excess is refunded to the method of the payment being refunded within refund_processing_business_days business days, one refund per payment and never more than that payment.
